title: OpenAI ChatCompletions compatibility adapter with telemetry-enriched streaming & deterministic structured-output mapping
creator: Riley Chen
description:
Goal: Build a compatibility adapter that accepts incoming requests shaped like the OpenAI Chat Completions API and translates them into Redwood runtime calls while preserving: (1) streaming behavior, (2) function/tool calling semantics, and (3) deterministic structured-output enforcement. The adapter must also inject lightweight telemetry hooks (token-level events and high-level outcome signals) so the Console can surface compatibility deltas and latency/cost breakdowns.

Scope and constraints:
- Input: OpenAI ChatCompletions request objects (messages, top_p/temperature, n, stop, functions schema, function_call hints and name). Must support both blocking and streaming flows.
- Output: Redwood internal request shape with explicit stream framing. For compatibility, the adapter will produce response shapes that mimic OpenAI event types ("delta" tokens, "finish_reason", and function call objects) when used in OpenAI-compat mode.
- Streaming: implement SSE-like framed events for downstream clients while using Redwood streaming transport internally. Must support client disconnects and backpressure without poisoning runtime resources.
- Function calling: translate OpenAI functions[] into our tool registry lookup. For auto-invoke vs. suggested function decisions, respect original OpenAI semantics (function_call: "auto"/"none"/"{name}") and produce function_call invocation objects in streamed deltas. Provide a deterministic fallback when a tool is unavailable (fallback policy with explicit signal in the stream).
- Structured outputs: when a function/schema is provided, validate output JSON against provided schema and emit structured_output events (and structured output diagnostics) in the stream if validation fails. Add a deterministic post-processing step to coerce minor issues (e.g., missing optional fields) with an audit signal.
- Telemetry: emit token-level timing and token counts as metadata (non-customer PII). Tag compatibility translations and mapping deltas so Console can alert on behavioral differences. Ensure telemetry can be toggled per-customer for privacy.

Design decisions and trade-offs:
- Translation layer vs. gateway: we implement an in-service adapter (middleware) rather than a long-lived standalone gateway to reduce cross-service latency and allow using existing runtime circuit breakers. Trade-off: slightly larger binary and more surface area in runtime service but lower end-to-end latency.
- Determinism for function calls: when ambiguous, favor conservative behavior (do not auto-invoke when model signal is weak). This reduces spurious tool usage at the cost of occasionally requiring an extra model loop to confirm invocation.
- Framing: adopt an event envelope that mirrors OpenAI-completions events but attach a stable "compat_version" field so we can evolve format without breaking downstream tooling.

Implementation plan:
1. Middleware scaffold: HTTP route /v1/compat/chat.completions that validates incoming OpenAI payloads and normalizes fields.
2. Stream shaper: translate Redwood streaming tokens into OpenAI-style delta events. Implement graceful drain and client disconnect handling.
3. Function-call resolver: map OpenAI function definitions to our tool IDs; implement a registry lookup with capability flags and quick-fail responses.
4. Structured validator: JSON Schema validator run post-generation with a configurable "coerce" flag; emit diagnostics events into stream.
5. Telemetry hooks: token timing, downstream mapping deltas, function-invocation traces. Expose events to Console via metrics + trace logs.
6. Backwards compatibility tests and Golden responses: create a harness that replays a curated set of OpenAI example conversations and asserts the emitted event sequence.

Testing & QA:
- Unit tests for request normalization and field-presence permutations (role/name/system, attachments like content-type variations).
- Integration tests covering streaming interleaving with function calls, including tool timeouts and partial results.
- Regression suite that runs against an OpenAI reference shim for behavioral diffs (delta sequence and finish_reason equivalence).
- Load test to measure added latency at p95/p99 when adapter enabled.

Rollout and monitoring:
- Feature-flag the endpoint per-customer. Start with internal Redwood accounts and a handful of low-risk customers.
- Canary rollout: 5% -> 25% -> 100% with performance and correctness gates in Console (token-level latency, function-call mismatch rate, validation error rate).
- SLOs: add alert if compatibility-layer adds >20ms median or >50ms p95 to baseline or if function-call mismatch rate >1%.

Artifacts and links:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/OpenAI+ChatCompletions+Compatibility+Adapter
- GH prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1234
- Structured-output test corpus: gs://redwood-testdata/compatibility/openai-struct-tests

Open questions / borderline decisions:
- Should the adapter rewrite user-supplied stop sequences to a unified format? (Currently plan: normalize whitespace but not semantics.)
- How to expose partial function-call arguments during streaming? (Plan: stream function_call.name early and payload at end to avoid inconsistent tool triggers.)
- Backpressure policy tunables: need input from infra on token queue limits for dedicated vs hosted deployments.

Acceptance criteria:
- Adapter passes all Golden harnesses with <0.5% behavioral diffs vs our reference mapping.
- Streaming clients observe OpenAI-compatible event ordering and finish_reason signals.
- Function calls invoked only when model signal meets threshold; registry failures produce explicit compatibility fallback events.
- Telemetry events appear in Console and are toggleable at the tenant level.

Future work (out-of-scope for this ticket):
- Schema evolution tooling that auto-suggests compatibility patches when mismatches are observed in production.
- SDK helpers to convert raw OpenAI streams into native SDK events for major client languages.
